newsitem.title: USA: U.S. foreign crudes add to domestic surplus.
newsitem.headline: U.S. foreign crudes add to domestic surplus.

text.p: U.S. foreign crudes were seen adding to the surplus of domestic grades, evidenced by bloated stocks last week and emerging offers for September.
Traders were surprised by the large builds in overall U.S. crude oil, blaming the influx on higher short-haul cargoes and more trans-Atlantic shipments than expected.
Some 40 percent of Sullom Voe liftings in the week ended Aug 27 were headed for the U.S., further weighing on domestic grades in the mid-term, traders said.
Latest U.S. inventory data also showed a 10 million build in crude stocks nationwide for the week ended Aug 23.
Oct West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was at $21.70-80 a barrel late Wednesday, up 30 cents from Tuesday.
Outright prices staged a recovery from the depths plumbed after the surprising U.S. crude stock build, traders said.
Meanwhile, a U.K. refiner offered Brent into the U.S. Gulf around WTI minus 10 cents for early-Oct cif.
Other North Sea offers included Oseberg for late-September near the same level.
From Latin America, Cusiana was offered for lifting second-half September at Nov WTI minus five to 10 cents fob.
Oriente was also available for mid-September, and asked at WTI minus $1.75 cif.
Chile's state firm ENAP bought a second cargo of Oriente at five cents over Petroecuador's formula for Oct 15-18 arrival, and 960,000 barrels of Escravos against Dated Brent.
In the aftermarket, October paper Brent traded at $20.30.
